A law that everyone quietly ignores can be more corrosive than no law at all. When a rule is kept on the books but never enforced, it does not simply lie dormant; it teaches citizens that the written word and the real world need not match. Each unpunished breach makes the next one easier to excuse, and over time the habit of selective obedience spreads to rules that were meant to bind. The damage lies less in the single ignored statute than in the lesson it spreads about how seriously any law should be taken.

To credit a single mind, then, is to mistake the visible tip of a long collective effort for the whole of it.

A score, then, summarises not the product alone but the peculiar crowd that chose to judge it, and reading it wisely means asking who did the rating before trusting what they said.
